name: River Pointe
title: Window Cleaning in River Pointe, Lake Austin | CleanzATX
description: Window cleaning for River Pointe, the Lake Austin estate enclave inside Glenlake. Pure water, poles to three stories, $10 per window. Text for a quote.
h1_em: on the banks of Lake Austin.
intro: River Pointe is a Lake Austin estate enclave inside Glenlake, with about 30 homes on acreage lots along the water. CleanzATX cleans windows here with pure water and poles, and Tyler quotes every home himself.

sections.h2: What River Pointe homes are like
paragraphs: River Pointe is a small group of roughly 30 homes within the Glenlake area, and every lot is big. Parcels run from about 1.6 to 4.35 acres, and they sit on the banks of Lake Austin, many with private docks. Homes were built between 1993 and 2012, so you see a mix of earlier custom houses and newer builds, with values from about $1M up to $6M. It is not gated and there is no HOA listed, which means each owner decides how the property is kept up. Long drives, mature trees and large lawns running toward the water are the norm.
With this much land, a house often has several wings, a guest house or a separate boat house to look after.

sections.h2: What River Pointe windows deal with
paragraphs: Waterfront acreage is hard on glass. Lake spray and humid air leave a mineral film, irrigation for big lawns throws hard water against the lower panes, and the sun off the water makes every smudge visible. White mineral spots can etch glass if left for years, so we treat them early. Our pure water system, a dual RO with 4 stage filtration and a DI resin tank, delivers water near 0 TDS. That dries clear with no soap film, which matters most on large panes that face the water.

Mature trees bring spider webs, leaf litter and pollen into screens and tracks. Cedar pollen runs December to February and live oak pollen March and April. Tracks and screens are each $5, and hard water spot removal is $10 per pane.

Houses this size are scheduled with care. We confirm the window count by text, then plan a visit with the exterior glass done from the ground with water fed poles that reach up to three stories. With 200 gallons of water on board we do not depend on your spigot for pressure work, which helps on long drives. Interior glass is by hand with drop cloths. Soft wash for stone and stucco, and flatwork for terraces and drives, can ride along on one trip. We are careful about dock decks and ask first before touching anything near the water.
For a 6,000 sq ft home, exterior windows at $0.10 per sq ft are about $600. Expect roughly four and a half to six hours outside and around three hours inside. Doing both sides runs $15 per window.

why: Lake spray, irrigation and water glare all show on big waterfront panes.
Acreage lots mean long drives, so we carry our own 200 gallons.
We ask before working near docks and the water edge.
Pure water dries clear on very large panes facing the lake.

faq.q: Do you work on Lake Austin waterfront homes?
faq.a: Yes. River Pointe is on the lake, and we clean exterior glass from the ground with water fed poles. We text before arriving and use pure water so panes dry without spots.

faq.q: My house has more than one building. How is that priced?
faq.a: Exterior windows are $10 per window ($5 per pane), or about $0.10 per sq ft of the home. For guest houses and boat houses, send photos and a count, and we quote the whole property by text.

faq.q: Do you clean glass near the dock?
faq.a: We work the windows on the buildings. For anything on or over the water we ask first and keep clear of docks unless you tell us what you need and we agree it is safe.

faq.q: Can you wash the patios and stone around the pool?
faq.a: Yes. Patios and pool decks are cleaned by hand so they do not get soaked, and limestone is soft washed only. Concrete is $0.18 per sq ft and pavers are $0.25, with a $250 minimum.

faq.q: Do you need power or water from the house?
faq.a: No. Our 8 ft skid carries 200 gallons of water on board, and the window system makes its own pure water, so we do not draw heavily on your spigot.
